newsitem.title: UK: End-April OECD oil stocks above year earlier - IEA.
newsitem.headline: End-April OECD oil stocks above year earlier - IEA.

text.p: Oil stocks held by industry in countries of the Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) were 2,439 million barrels at the end of April, some 106 million barrels above year earlier levels, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
The level was only 3 million barrels under April 1995 which was the highest end-April stock level in the 1990s, the IEA said in it's latest Monthly Oil Market Report.
Gasoline is the only fuel for which current OECD stocks are less than year earlier levels, the difference being just 5 million barrels.
Distillate stocks were 47 million higher than a year ago and crude oil stocks exceeded year earlier levels by 32 million barrels.
Residual fuel and other oil stocks were 16 million and 18 million respectively higher than last year.
During April total OECD stocks rose by 0.8 million barrels per day (bpd) led by higher crude oil stocks in all three major OECD regions.
Total OECD crude oil stocks were 32 million barrels higher at the end of April than at the end of March, while product stocks declined by about 100,000 bpd.
A rise of 200,000 bpd in crude oil stocks in the Pacific region was reinforced by a gain of just under 300,000 bpd in product and other oil stocks.
But in Europe a 500,000 bpd crude stockbuild was more than offset by falling product stocks.
Product and other oil stocks rose marginally in North America but by an amount that was less than one-third of the 200,000 bpd crude oil stocks build.

In North America the stock situation continues to be mixed with low and declining gasoline stocks giving the market support while high and growing crude oil, residual and to a lesser extent distillate stocks are having a depressing effect on prices.

Very high refinery runs and significant imports of oil products are expected to keep stocks high through 2Q97. The small fall in European stocks was due to gains in the Netherlands and France being more than offset by inventory falls in Italy, the UK, Germany and the rest of OECD Europe.

Crude oil stocks rose in all countries except the UK while distillates stock fell in all countries except France. The Netherlands was the only one of the major oil consuming countries where residual fuel and gasoline stocks rose.
In the Pacific Region the stockbuild was led by builds in "other" oils which rose by 270,000 bpd. Crude rose 210,000 bpd while distillates rose 180,000 bpd.
